quote: Santosh Kumar Verma tells us that the provisions of the *akshayanivi* (permanent-endowment) system for the management of religious institutions appear in the Satavahana period. Evidence of their extensive allotment of agricultural land, too, begins to be found — the first mention of which is in the inscriptions of Gautamiputra Satakarni and in the accounts of the Chutu rulers, who gave such donations to the *viharas* of Nagarjunakonda and Amaravati. In the Gupta period their number began to grow, where various Smriti-writers and text-authors mentioned *akshayanivi* in the form of wealth and, in later times, *nidhi*, *nyasa* and *nikshepa*. In the south, too, it was in vogue. After the Gupta period, land-donations were given to temples on a large scale — and that with special privileges such as '*sa-dandashapa-aparadha*' and '*bhutopata-pratyaya*', which was, in one way or another, indeed to some extent a transfer of the absolute exclusive rights of the royal power.
